# Disagreement Log — Didache Chapter 9

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Didache 9 — The Eucharist (First Prayer)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 6

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.2-3: παῖς — "servant" vs. "child"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "servant" |
| LOGOS | "servant" |
| PNEUMA | "servant" |

**Issue:** παῖς = both servant and child. The Isaianic Servant Song background strongly favors "servant." However, the "child of God" dimension is present, especially in relation to Jesus. All agents agree on "servant."
**Ruling:** "Servant" unanimous. Translator note preserves the double meaning.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: "vine of David" — what does this mean?

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "holy vine of David your servant" |
| LOGOS | "holy vine of David your servant" |
| PNEUMA | "holy vine of your servant David" |

**Issue:** Greek word order: τῆς ἁγίας ἀμπέλου Δαυὶδ τοῦ παιδός σου = "the holy vine of David your servant." PNEUMA reorders to "vine of your servant David." The Greek places "David" as the genitive of the vine and "your servant" as an appositive to David.
**Ruling:** "Vine of David your servant" (EMET/LOGOS) adopted. This preserves the Greek's appositive structure.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.3: "life and knowledge" — translation of ζωή καὶ γνῶσις

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "the life and knowledge" |
> LOGOS | "the life and knowledge" |
| PNEUMA | "the life and knowledge" |

**Issue:** No disagreement. All agents translate ζωή καὶ γνῶσις as "life and knowledge." Noted: this is not the Gnostic γνῶσις but the knowledge of God given through the gospel (cf. John 17:3).
**Ruling:** "Life and knowledge" unanimous.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.4: κλάσμα — "broken bread" rendering and expansion

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "as this broken bread was scattered upon the mountains" |
| LOGOS | "as this broken bread was scattered over the mountains" |
| PNEUMA | "scattered across the mountains — grain growing on hillside after hillside" |

**Issue:** PNEUMA's expansion ("grain growing on hillside after hillside") adds the agricultural back-story implied by "scattered on mountains" (grain grows in the mountains, is harvested, milled, baked into bread). The image in the Greek is already extraordinary without expansion.
**Ruling:** "Scattered upon the mountains" (EMET/LOGOS) retained without expansion. The image's power lies in its concision.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.4: "Church" capitalization

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "your church" (lowercase) |
| LOGOS | "your Church" (capitalized) |
| PNEUMA | "your Church" (capitalized) |

**Issue:** ἐκκλησία = the assembled people of God. In a eucharistic prayer context, capitalization ("Church") signals the theological dimension of the gathered community. Given the eschatological context ("from the ends of the earth"), capitalization is appropriate.
**Ruling:** "Your Church" (capitalized) adopted (LOGOS/PNEUMA).

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.5: "Do not give what is holy to the dogs" — quoting style

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | Quoted with "the Lord also said" |
| LOGOS | Quoted with "the Lord himself has said" |
| PNEUMA | Quoted with "The Lord himself said it" |

**Issue:** Minor stylistic variation. "The Lord himself has said" (LOGOS) carries both the emphatic (αὐτός = himself) and the stative perfect force.
**Ruling:** "The Lord himself has said" (LOGOS) adopted.
